text:
Ivy: Noticed confusion in dashboards: legend labels don't show units while y-axis does. During demos customers asked whether numbers were % or absolute.
Priya: Oh yes. Suggest a small unit chip next to the label, e.g. 'Errors • req/s' or a muted chip 'req/s'.
Luis: Chips are good but watch overflow on narrow screens. Current legend is horizontally scrollable so chips could push layout.
Marta: Accessibility: chips need readable text at 14px and an aria-label like 'Errors, requests per second'. Don't rely on color alone.
DesignAssistant: Also ensure the chip meets contrast AA and is reachable via keyboard. If truncated, surface full text in a tooltip and announce via aria-live on focus.
Priya: UX option: show chip inline on wide screens, fallback to secondary row 'unit' under label when space constrained. Mobile: show chip on tap.
Ivy: Another related nit: smoothing control sitting in the legend toolbar is easy to miss. Move smoothing to an overflow menu with a visible 'Curve' affordance on hover.
Luis: If we move it, announce state changes: 'Curve enabled for Errors' using a live region. Quick snippet: const announce = msg => { liveRegion.textContent = msg }
Marta: Accessibility checklist: overflow menu keyboard focusable, menu items have aria-checked state, caption linked via aria-describedby to chart.
Priya: Decision: add unit chip + overflow menu for controls + helper copy for outlier handling. I'll update the component spec and mock both inline chip and secondary-row variants.
